title.narrative: Multi-Sector Anticipatory Interventions (MSAI) in Dassenech and Bena-Tsemay Districts

description.narrative: ltpgtThe overall objective of this Anticipatory Action is to provide assistance before the drought’s full impact is felt, protecting livelihoods and preventing a nutrition crisis to vulnerable communities (Host, IDPs and returnees) in Benatsemay and Dassenech Woredas of South Omo Zone, South Ethiopia Region. Agriculture and WASH sectors are considered in this Anticipatory Action mainstreaming protection, Early warning and other cross-cuttingnbspinterventions to reach a total of 12,632 HHs ornbsp75,792 direct beneficiaries (24,558 men, 20,916 women, 16,368 boys and 13,950nbspgirls). From the total targeted beneficiaries, 990 are persons with disabilities. The proposed anticipatory action will not only focus on services provision but also focuses on integrated and multi sector interventions to contribute to the reduction of malnutrition. Coordination will be made with Health and Nutrition sectors, Doctors with Africa CUAMM, in two Woredas ensuring beneficiaries are receiving benefits from multiple-sectors in an integrated way contributing towards reducing malnutrition, protecting livelihood, alleviating human suffering as well as promoting human wellbeing. The anticipatory project proposed under Agriculture, WASH and cash for work will be implemented by VSF Germany in both woredas. The pre-identified anticipatory activities of this project are designed to contribute to protect livelihoods and prevention of nutrition crisis to vulnerable people or groups mainly women, girls, children, people with disabilities and others with special needs by employing approaches like gender sensitive, Do No Harm, inclusive project implementation to the anticipated poor rains during the October – December 2024 in Dassenech and BenaTsemay Woredas of South Omo Zone, South Ethiopia Region. ltbrgtThe Agriculture sector intervention will have the following key components: support to Agro-pastoralist with early maturing crops and vegetables production to address their household food and income needs through provision of farming inputs such as improved seeds, tools, fodder seed, extension training services pastoralists through veterinary support (vaccination, animal treatment, livestock feeding, browse aid PEG-4000 training services).nbsp Whereas WASH interventions will help to improve inclusive access to protected water sources,nbsptraining on sanitation and hygiene practice and adopt good hygiene practices through support in the rehabilitations/upgrading of water schemes, Provision of NFIs,nbspwater treatment chemical supply including awareness creation hygiene sanitation. In both woredas, agro-pastoralists and pastoralists will be targeted for the cash for work activities including rangeland and livestock ponds rehabilitations. The anticipatory action will provide capacity building on Early warning focusing on preparedness/mitigation of the anticipated poor rains and its consequences with mainstreaming of protection. ltbrgtlt/pgt
